\subsection{Request-generation cost on a larger graph}
\label{app:arxiv-selector-cost}
On ogbn-arxiv (169,343 nodes), we use a random 70/10/20 split with seed 2024, rather than the official temporal split, and select 5,927 nodes from 118,540 training candidates (5\%). R-point, D-full, and fixed-budget IM-RR with 4,096 and 16,384 samples produced complete requests with the required size, uniqueness, candidate membership, and input identity verified. IM uses selector seed 11 and propagation probability 0.1; D-full retains the gt\_full GCN configuration and training seed 42. IM sampling and greedy coverage execute entirely on the CPU, without model training or GPU acceleration. R-point and D-full use the GPU for model/gradient computation and include CPU processing. These experiments evaluate request generation only; they contain no large-graph GU or retraining outcomes.

Selector-entry time includes current request access and verification; for R-point and D-full it also includes model preparation. Whole-job time is measured between Core start and finish and excludes queue and return. Successful IM runs invoked the Selection producer on a MISS; R-point and D-full had Checkpoint/Score/Selection MISS. The RR=65,536 run reached its 7,200-second limit without a complete trusted output; its 7,202-second wall includes termination overhead. RR=16,384 completed normally at 6,511 seconds, crossing the pre-agreed 6,480-second expansion-stop threshold. CPU model and thread allocation were not normalized; code/Core versions differ across runs. The table is not a controlled hardware or speedup comparison.
